newsitem.title: UK: Britain to mark 50 years of Indian independence.
newsitem.headline: Britain to mark 50 years of Indian independence.

text.p: Britain will mark the 50th anniversary of independence of India and Pakistan this year with a programme designed to emphasise the history and traditions that still link it to the Asian subcontinent, a cabinet minister said on Monday.

"We have been friends with the peoples of the sub-continent for centuries. Our present relations have never been better or more productive. They are based on a shared history and shared traditions: parliamentary government, the rule of law, cricket," Lord Robert Cranborne, Leader of the upper House of Lords, said in a statement.
The celebrations will begin with a government banquet on honour of India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh on March 11, he said.
That will be followed by a midsummer reception in the Houses of Parliament, and a reception on June 13 hosted by heir to the throne Prince Charles.

In addition, Queen Elizabeth, who is already scheduled to visit India and Pakistan in October, will invite a higher than usual proportion of Britain's Asian community to her annual Buckingham Palace garden parties this year.

Ordinary Britons will be introduced to subcontinental culture through events ranging from a Mughal Tent Textiles Exhibition in a London museum to the performance of plays based on the Hindu epic the Mahabharata.
Cranborne said the government also wanted to recognise the sacrifice of people of the sub-continent who fought alongside British troops in two world wars with a memorial in London.
"During the Second World War, the Indian Army contained not a single conscript...and the wartime Indian Army was the largest volunteer force ever assembled," he recalled.
In a message of support for the programme, Prince Charles paid tribute "to the enormous contribution made by the peoples of the sub-continent to British life".
